items.summary: Kernel optimization is essential for efficient large language model (LLM) training and inference on Ascend NPUs. Existing Ascend kernel benchmarks primarily focus on kernel generation, with less emphasis on the ability of agents to optimize existing implementations under input configurations drawn from real workloads. items.title: Weight-Space Programming Doesn't Need Transformers
items.summary: Standard neural architectures such as the Transformer were chosen because they train well with gradient descent and run fast on GPUs. In weight-space programming, a large language model (LLM) writes target weights by hand without gradient-based training, so those reasons no longer apply. Should we keep the Transformer? items.title: Multi-Branch Transformer
items.summary: Transformer language models are commonly scaled by making their blocks wider or stacking them deeper. In this work, we explore a complementary path: branching, the parallel composition of full Transformer blocks. We introduce the Multi-Branch Transformer (MBT), which processes the input through shared initial layers, executes independently parameterized branches of sequential blocks in parallel, and fuses their outputs before shared final layers.

items.summary: Most AI assistants respond only when prompted, remaining silent even when events in the video stream offer meaningful opportunities for conversation. To move beyond purely user-driven interaction, we present AURA 2.0, a streaming video large language model that introduces three core upgrades to AURA. items.summary: Electronic nose (eNose) technology offers a portable, non-invasive route for disease screening via exhaled breath analysis. items.summary: Harness optimization is often studied with a fixed policy model and benchmark. items.summary: Collaboration promises to extend humanoid capabilities beyond what individual robots can achieve. items.summary: Interactive video world models enable exploration through text and camera controls, yet direct object interaction requires finer control. items.summary: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate frames based on new observations and inputs, making them a promising medium for interactive visual experiences. items.summary: Understanding long videos requires locating evidence, resolving visual details, and integrating observations into an answer. items.summary: Medical image understanding with vision-language models (VLMs) typically relies on autoregressively generating reasoning and answer tokens. items.summary: Looping is a powerful inductive bias for reasoning. items.summary: Robots in homes, warehouses and farms must pick up objects they have never seen, usually without a 3D model or a category label. items.summary: CAD practitioners often work with proprietary parts that they are unwilling to share with external services.
